thread.title_full: Bipartisan bill proposes new flag honoring families affected by veteran suicide

author: Scranton Reporter
title: Bipartisan bill proposes new flag honoring families affected by veteran suicide
text:
U.S. Representatives Rob Bresnahan, Jr. (PA-08) and Madeleine Dean (PA-04) have introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at honoring the families of veterans who have died by suicide. The proposed Sgt. Walter F. Hartnett IV Green Star Veterans Service Act would require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to create an official Green Star flag for the next of kin of these veterans.
The bill is named after Sergeant Walter F. Hartnett IV, a servicemember whose death was attributed to what lawmakers described as “the invisible wounds of war.” The initiative seeks to provide recognition and comfort to families affected by veteran suicide.
Rep. Bresnahan said, “We honor those who gave their lives for our country on the battlefield, but we cannot forget those who lost their lives to the lasting wounds of service. Veterans Day is a crucial reminder of the courage, dedication, and sacrifice of each veteran, including those who lose their lives to suicide. The Green Star flag will serve as a visible reminder that these veterans and their families’ sacrifices matter and that our nation stands beside them.”
Rep. Dean added, “Walt Hartnett was a man devoted to service — to his country, his fellow veterans, his Conshohocken community, and, above all, his beautiful family. I was blessed to work alongside him, and our office was better because of his powerful voice for veterans in need. He led an expansive life, one that we lost too soon to suicide. Every day, we lose an estimated 22 veterans to suicide — men and women who gave of themselves entirely for our freedom, and who bore wounds civilians cannot fathom. Yet, their families receive no federal recognition for such excruciating loss. The Sgt. Walter F. Hartnett IV Green Star Veterans Service Act would change that by creating a Green Star Service flag to raise awareness of the crisis of veteran suicide and provide resources for their loved ones. I thank my fellow Pennsylvanian, Congressman Rob Bresnahan, for co-leading this important and personal bipartisan bill.”
Matt Cahill from Green Star Families of America commented on the significance: “Families who have lost a Veteran to suicide deserve their own place of honor, not hidden under any other banner, and no longer overlooked,” he said.“The Green Star Service Banner affirms that their loss matters, their service endures, and their strength will forever stand as part of America’s storied legacy of service and sacrifice.”
The legislation emphasizes efforts toward reducing stigma around mental health issues within military communities while aiming to ensure every veteran’s legacy receives appropriate acknowledgment.
